issue.title: Chains do not work with nested groups
issue.body:
I seem to have stumbled across a bug in the chain implementation. Given the following tasks:

```
from time import sleep

import celery

@celery.task
def source_generate():
    sleep(1.0)
    print "SourceGenerate"
    return "source"

@celery.task
def source_upload(source):
    sleep(1.0)
    print "SourceUpload: %s" % (source,)

@celery.task
def derivative_source_generate(source):
    sleep(1.0)
    print "DerivativeSourceGenerate: %s" % (source,)
    return "derivative-source"

@celery.task
def derivative_convert(source, profile):
    sleep(1.0)
    print "DerivativeConvert: %s profile=%s" % (source, profile)
    return "derivative-%s" % (profile,)

@celery.task
def derivative_upload(source):
    sleep(1.0)
    print "DerivativeUpload: %s" % (source,)

@celery.task
def cleanup(results):
    print "Cleanup: %s" % (results,)
```

I can execute tasks like this without incident:

```
body = group(source_upload.s(), derivative_source_generate.s() | derivative_convert.s(profile='hq') | derivative_upload.s())
t = source_generate.s() | body | cleanup.s()
t.delay()
```

Everything looks great in the logs:

```
[2013-11-19 12:59:34,248: WARNING/Worker-8] SourceGenerate
[2013-11-19 12:59:35,280: WARNING/Worker-9] SourceUpload: source
[2013-11-19 12:59:35,290: WARNING/Worker-8] DerivativeSourceGenerate: derivative-source
[2013-11-19 12:59:36,296: WARNING/Worker-2] DerivativeConvert: derivative-source profile=hq
[2013-11-19 12:59:37,325: WARNING/Worker-4] DerivativeUpload: derivative-source
[2013-11-19 12:59:37,814: WARNING/Worker-3] CleanupTask: [None, 'derivative-hq']
```

However, when I introduce another group inside the `body`, the callback is never called:

```
body = group(source_upload.s(), derivative_source_generate.s() | \
    group(derivative_convert.s(profile='hq') | derivative_upload.s()))
t = source_generate.s() | body | cleanup.s()
t.delay()
```

And the logs:

```
[2013-11-19 12:59:34,248: WARNING/Worker-8] SourceGenerate
[2013-11-19 12:59:35,280: WARNING/Worker-9] SourceUpload: source
[2013-11-19 12:59:35,290: WARNING/Worker-8] DerivativeSourceGenerate: derivative-source
[2013-11-19 12:59:36,296: WARNING/Worker-2] DerivativeConvert: derivative-source profile=hq
[2013-11-19 12:59:37,325: WARNING/Worker-4] DerivativeUpload: derivative-source
```

I require this functionality in my application as my workflow needs to have multiple `derivative_convert.s() | derivative_upload.s()` chains for different profiles being generated from a single file. 

The main thing is that I believe I've discovered a bug in the chain implementation, as chains don't continue if there exists a group within a group somewhere in the chain body. 

I'm happy to invest the time to fix this, but I'm not sure what's going wrong or where things are getting stuck in Celery.

body: Does your fix work? Do you plan on opening a pull request?
It works.  It's in this PR: https://github.com/celery/celery/pull/2226

I wasn't able to fix all of the nesting problems, however.  I tried some exploratory fixes, but they didn't work.

After reviewing the code, I think I understand where the bugs are coming from.  It's due to problems in serializing and deserializing taskmessage objects.  Most of the problems I addressed were due to deserialization issues (when the worker reconstructs the message from the backend), however, there are still some _serialization issues_ (when the client writes the taskmessage to the backend).

See the tests in https://github.com/aneilbaboo/celery_async_issue.  I'm seeing failures in `test_complex_nesting` and `test_group_in_chain_in_group`.   Just follow the install instructions and run nosetests.  You should see an Exception 'EncodeError: keys must be a string' inside celery.app.amqp.publish_task.  

I think these signature nesting bugs keep cropping up because we don't have a way to cleanly serialize and deserialize  signatures.   It seems that the code for sending a task message to the queue is intertwined with the logic that constructs the task message.  It would be great if these two bits of logic were cleanly separated, as this would allow us to write unit tests.  I didn't fully grok the logic of what's going on, so I was apprehensive to undertake this myself.

issue.title: .get() method not blocking properly with upgraded chords - v3.1.23
issue.body:
I am experiencing an issue where the .get() method is not waiting for the chord to complete. 

The chord has been upgraded from a chain, as the group is chained with normal tasks. An example of this chain layout is below:

```
job = chain( 
    group(blah.si(), blah2.si()),

    normal_task.si(),

    group(blah3.s(), blah4.s()),

    normal_task_2.si(),
    normal_task_3.si()
).delay()

```

When running this code followed by job.get(), an AsyncResult object is returned immediately. The result of this is the value returned by the task normal_task (the second step above). If I alter the chain to just include just a group, just tasks, or a group followed by a task, .get() waits and blocks as expected. It seems that multiple nested groups and tasks are causing an issue.

I noticed the following issue but it looks like a fix was implemented. Has a bug been reintroduced here? https://github.com/celery/celery/issues/2228.

Thanks!

issue.title: Last item in chain not referenced if preceded by Chord
issue.body:
## Overview

Given two sample tasks:

``` python
@shared_task
def add(x, y):
    return x + y

@shared_task
def total(values):
    return sum(values)
```

And the following test case:

``` python
from celery import group
from tasks import add, total

c1 = add.s(4, 4)  # Single Task
c2 = c1 | add.s(3)  # Chain of Task + Task
c3 = group(c1, c1, c1)  # Group of three Tasks
c4 = c3 | total.s()  # Chord of Group + Task
c5 = c4 | add.s(1)  # Chain of Chord + Task
c6 = c5 | add.s(1)  # Chain of Chord + Task + Task
c7 = c6 | add.s(1)  # Chain of Chord + Task + Task + Task
```

I observe the following:

``` python
In [10]: c4.apply_async().get()  # Expect 24
Out[10]: 24

In [11]: c5.apply_async().get()  # Expect 25
Out[11]: 24

In [12]: c6.apply_async().get()  # Expect 26
Out[12]: 26

In [13]: c7.apply_async().get()  # Expect 27
Out[13]: 27
```

Thus, when the chord is the penultimate item in a chain with a Redis broker, calling `apply_async()` returns the Task ID of the chord, instead of the final task in the chain. This is exemplified by `c5` expecting a value of `25`, but getting `24` instead.
## Workaround

I can get around this by adding a dummy / identity task which simply returns its argument, so the chord is not the penultimate task.
## Notes

This is claimed to be fixed by #2226 but given that it is still being observed in v3.1.23, the issue remains.

Similar to #2228 and #3137. Tested with v3.1.18 and the latest v3.1.23. Observed with a Redis broker and a Django database backend.
